findings.finding: Clients often resist being told what to think, but engage more when asked questions.
findings.qualification: This finding is based on observed behavior and may not apply universally to all clients.

findings.finding: Dead leads can be valuable, as agencies may be sitting on missed opportunities worth millions.
findings.qualification: This is self-reported and hypothetical, requiring validation for broader applicability.

findings.finding: Implementing a structured follow-up calendar for rejected clients can improve engagement.
findings.qualification: The impact may vary based on the efficacy of the follow-up strategy.

findings.finding: Systematic nurturing of dead leads over time can result in closed deals.
findings.qualification: Nurturing efforts must be consistent and targeted for effective results.

findings.finding: Bad leads are often blamed when clients disappear after initial meetings.
findings.qualification: This is self-reported and may be subjective, not accounting for other factors causing client disengagement.

findings.finding: Self-reflection on mistakes can help agents improve their client interactions.
findings.qualification: The efficacy of self-reflection as a strategy is hypothetical and varies among agents.

findings.finding: Sales can falter in the follow-up stages or when agents aren't controlling presentations.
findings.qualification: This is an observed claim requiring more systematic study to confirm its prevalence.

findings.finding: Understanding client buying potential is crucial for improving sales outcomes.
findings.qualification: Strategies for assessing client potential are not detailed in the evidence, limiting specificity.
